questions: What is the correct CLI command structure for a no-flag lifecycle action?
How should the CLI handle the { ok: true } response from the resume endpoint?

answers.answer: Follow the terminate.ts pattern but without flags: new resume.ts file exports cmdGoalsResume(config, goalId) that POSTs to /goals/:id/resume with empty body. The goals/index.ts switch gets a new 'resume' case that validates goalId and calls the function. Help text includes the resume usage.
evidence: src/goals/terminate.ts — cmdGoalsTerminate: hxFetch POST, parseApiError, console.log display
src/goals/index.ts:57-68 — terminate case: help check, goalId validation, call command

answers.answer: Display a simple confirmation message ('Goal resumed successfully') with the goalId. The server returns { ok: true } which confirms the action succeeded. Unlike terminate (which returns the goal object with id, title, status), resume returns a boolean acknowledgment. The CLI should display the goalId it was given.
evidence: Server tech research — resume endpoint returns { ok: true }, not the goal object

statement: The CLI resume implementation adds a new resume.ts file following the terminate.ts pattern: POST to /goals/:id/resume with empty body, display confirmation. A new 'resume' case in goals/index.ts and updated CLI docs in cli-content.ts complete the change. No flags needed, no new dependencies.
